# kdbxweb (vendored)

[kdbxweb](https://github.com/keeweb/kdbxweb) by Antelle, MIT (see `LICENSE`). Git state `UPSTREAM_COMMIT` (2.2.0, npm stops at 2.1.1).

Eight local fixes and one addition, all already applied in `lib/`. The diffs in `patches/` record what changed, so it can be carried
over after an update. They are not uniform: seven are `git diff` output with different path prefixes (`a/lib/...` or
`a/vendor/kdbxweb/lib/...`, and `date-overflow-fix.patch` doesn't apply cleanly to `UPSTREAM_COMMIT` as it is), `xml-tab-fix.patch` and
`history-customdata-fix.patch` are plain `diff` output. Read them as a list of changes to redo, not as something to feed to
`git apply`. A comparison of `lib/` with `UPSTREAM_COMMIT` (second review of 0.18.0) found exactly these changes and nothing else.

- `enable-searching-fix.patch`: write missing optional group fields as defaults instead of empty elements, which KeePassXC rejects.
- `xml-tab-fix.patch`: keep the tab character (0x09) when cleaning XML. It's valid in XML 1.0, upstream dropped it.
- `lastmodtime-binary-fix.patch`: in KDBX 4.1, write `LastModificationTime` of custom icons and custom data as binary (Base64)
  like every other KDBX 4 timestamp, text only in XML export. Same change as upstream PR #62 (issue #49), still open there.
- `history-customdata-fix.patch`: `KdbxEntry.copyFrom` also copies custom data and the quality-check flag, so history items and
  merged entries keep them (KeePassXC fixed the same for its own history items in 2.8.0, #13573).
- `date-overflow-fix.patch`: read binary timestamps without `Int64.value`, which threw "too large number" on the huge "never" values some apps (KeePassDX) write, and cap them at the latest date .NET can represent. Upstream fixed the same in keenext/kdbxweb.
- `twofish.patch`: Twofish-256 as a third cipher next to AES and ChaCha20 (`lib/crypto/twofish.ts`, written from the 1998
  specification), so files KeePassXC encrypted with Twofish open and save. Upstream never had it.
- `aes-rounds-limit.patch`: `KeyEncryptorAes.encrypt` refuses more than 1 000 000 000 rounds (`KdbxError` `Unsupported`, "too many aes rounds"). The round count comes from the file header; the app asks before opening files over 100 million rounds (`src/core/kdf-policy.js`) and this is the limit behind that question.
- `merge-tombstones-fix.patch`: `Kdbx.merge` no longer treats every tombstone as final, and no longer purges custom icons. Upstream skipped every item with a tombstone before comparing any times, so an entry deleted for good on one device and changed later on the other was lost. Now deleted items are merged like the others, then the tombstones of both sides (one per object, the later deletion time) are applied to the merged tree, children first, like the synchronize mode of KeePass 2: an entry or group changed after its deletion stays and loses its tombstone, a group only goes once it is empty, times count in whole seconds. Unlike KeePass 2, a move counts as a change (restoring from the recycle bin only moves the entry). Icon tombstones work the same way against the icon's own time and the newest entry or group using it; references to a deleted icon are cleared, history included. And `merge()` no longer ends with `cleanup({ customIcons: true })`, which deleted every icon unused at that moment and wrote tombstones for them (library icons, icons the other side still uses); KeePass 2 and KeePassXC don't purge on merge either. Made on top of `enable-searching-fix.patch` (both touch `kdbx-group.ts`).
- `merge-moves-fix.patch`: `Kdbx.merge` puts every entry and group in exactly one group. Upstream compared the move times (`LocationChanged`) group by group, while `KdbxEntry.merge` and `KdbxGroup.merge` had already copied the newer side's times, move time included: an entry the other side moved into a group that gets merged earlier, and changed on the way (`keepassxc-cli mv` does), was kept by its old group as well. The same object sat in two groups, was saved twice, and every later merge failed on the duplicate UUID. Now `Kdbx.merge` decides up front, from the times before the merge, which objects go where the other side has them (moved there later), and each object keeps the move time of the place it ends up in, not the one that came with the newer content. A group only one side has is merged too: upstream skipped it, so the other side's changes to the entries in it were dropped, and an entry the other side moved out of it stayed in it as well. Groups the two sides moved into each other no longer form a loop that nothing reaches from the root (it vanished with everything in it): the group whose chosen place is the older one goes to its place on the other side, which both sides agree on. Made on top of `merge-tombstones-fix.patch`.
